A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, nine figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-descent experiments on the toy regression and interpolation problems, including learned functions in Figures 3c, 5, and 6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original gradient-descent outcomes in Figures 3c, 5, and 6, with experimental details in Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The network families, convex reformulations, and solution mappings are retained. The explicit free intercept in v2 Equation 8 reconciles the main text with the augmented-input formulation already present in v1 Proposition F.3, rather than introducing a new architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two-point regression and five-point interpolation examples. The higher-dimensional nonuniqueness constructions are also retained; no new empirical dataset, task, or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical comparison against competing methods. The additional citations in v2 support theoretical discussion rather than introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The toy experiments retain beta = 0.1, landscape visualizations for widths 1, 2, and 3, and gradient-descent demonstrations at widths 3/5 and 6/10. Their data construction and visualization procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The width-dependent landscape illustrations, learned-function comparisons, and geometric case studies are retained across the main text and appendices. No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both reproducibility statements report setting random seeds for initialization-dependent figures. Neither version supplies new run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The learned-function plots and empirical findings in Figures 3c, 5, and 6 are unchanged. The five-point example retains its reported optimal cost of 60. Figure 2's labeling changes do not change the displayed functions or outcomes.

T1.justification: v2 adds the sublevel-set connectivity corollary and proof (Corollary 3/D.2), nonzero-solution qualifications, and Proposition D.1. Theorem F.1 revises v1 Theorem G.1 to accommodate norms on subspaces and corrects the cone/unit-sphere union to a cone/unit-ball intersection. Other proof corrections refine the existing framework while retaining its principal characterizations and width thresholds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: dual characterization of optimal sets, the connectivity staircase, nonunique minimum-norm interpolators, and extensions to other architectures. Replacing 'counterexamples' with 'examples' does not change their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds an explicit interpretation of nonuniqueness outside the training data, noting that different optimal interpolators can diverge as inputs tend to infinity. Section 3.2 replaces the gradient-flow explanation with a cited nonincreasing-path existence argument.

D1.justification: v1 states that figure-generation code is provided without giving its location. v2 adds an explicit repository link in the Reproducibility Statement. The laptop, random-seed, and experimental-parameter disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Bucarelli et al. (2024) on topological complexity and Nakhleh et al. (2024) on interpolator uniqueness, plus references supporting path-existence arguments. Its central positioning relative to Mishkin and Pilanci and Boursier and Flammarion remains stable.

P1.justification: The main exposition is substantially reorganized: notation moves from Appendix A into Section 1.2, existing appendix propositions and corollaries enter the main text, and detailed theorem statements are shortened or deferred to appendices. Sections 2, 3.3, and 4.2 receive substantial explanatory rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts denser conference typesetting with different typography, spacing, headers, and extensive reflow and resizing of figures and equations. All nine figures remain; Figure 2 gains axis labels and a clearer caption, while figures such as Figures 4–5 are regrouped on the page.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through corrected definitions and explicit conditions, adds a proved sublevel-connectivity consequence, and makes notation and code access easier to find. These are useful refinements to the existing theoretical contribution, with unchanged empirical evidence. Denser typesetting and smaller figures modestly offset the gains in clarity and accessibility.
